question.text: Income from commodity futures settled through delivery is treated as:

answer.text: Business income arising from the purchase/sale of commodities — not as derivative trading income

explanation.text: The Logic: When a commodity futures contract is settled by physical delivery, the economic substance becomes the purchase or sale of the underlying commodity rather than a derivative-based settlement. Tax practice in India therefore treats the resulting income as business income from the purchase/sale of commodities — not as derivative trading income. The Trap: It is not capital gains (commodity trading is typically business in nature), it is not necessarily speculative (delivery-settled transactions are generally non-speculative), and it is certainly not tax-free. Note: The Series XVI Commodity Derivatives workbook pages reviewed cover delivery mechanics and accounting for exercised options, but do not state this specific income-tax classification rule. The framing above reflects general Indian income-tax practice for delivery-settled commodity derivatives.
